title: Leviticus: living near a holy God

lines: Leviticus begins where Exodus ends. The tent is built, and God's glory fills it, so that even Moses can't go in.
So here's the question. How can a holy God live among people who aren't holy, and the people live? This book is God's own answer.
I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be My people.

scripture.text: I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be My people.

lines: It has six parts. The offerings. The priests. Clean and unclean. The Day of Atonement, right at the center. Holiness in all of life. And vows.
The first half is about how to come near to God. The second is about how to live near him.

scripture.text: Be holy because I, the LORD your God, am holy.

lines: The Hebrew word for an offering means something brought near. There were five kinds, from the burnt offering given whole to the peace offering shared at a family meal.
God himself gives the means of atonement. And the poor could bring two birds, or flour.

scripture.text: the priest will make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.

lines: Clean and unclean are about being fit to come near the holy place. Unclean doesn't mean sinful. A new mother or a mourner had done nothing wrong, and it ended with time and washing.
No one should use this book to call another person dirty.

scripture.text: You must distinguish between the holy and the common

chapters.kicker: Watch for: the Day of Atonement
lines: Once a year the high priest, in plain linen, went behind the curtain into the Most Holy Place. And a goat carried the people's confessed sins away into the wilderness.
Jews still keep the day as Yom Kippur. Christians read it in the light of Jesus, as the book of Hebrews does.

scripture.text: because on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you

lines: Then holiness leaves the tent for the field, the court, and the shop. Leave the edges of your field for the poor. Pay wages the same day. Judge fairly. Love the foreigner, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
And at the center of it all:
Love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.

scripture.text: love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.

lines: All Christians read Leviticus as God's word, and none of them offer its sacrifices, because Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for all time. They differ on how its laws apply now.
On any reading, nothing here gives anyone a reason for contempt toward any person.
Start with chapters sixteen and nineteen. Then the key chapters: one, ten, eleven, seventeen, twenty-five, and twenty-six.
Read it as the working rules of a sacred house.
It asks what it would mean for a whole life to belong to God.
titleCard: A whole life that belongs to God.
